text: At the mans heels. <break time="0.8s" /> Trotted a dog. <break time="0.8s" /> A big gray husky. <break time="0.8s" /> That looked just like its brother. <break time="0.8s" /> The wild wolf. <break time="0.8s" /> The dog knew by instinct. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was no time for traveling. <break time="0.8s" /> For it was really. <break time="0.8s" /> Seventy five degrees below zero. <break time="0.8s" /> It walked close behind the man. <break time="0.8s" /> And watched his every move. <break time="0.8s" /> As if it expected him. <break time="0.8s" /> To stop and build a fire. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked carefully. <break time="0.8s" /> Along the frozen creek. <break time="0.8s" /> For he knew. <break time="0.8s" /> That some springs under the snow never froze. <break time="0.8s" /> Even in the coldest weather. <break time="0.8s" /> Once the dog broke through into the water. <break time="0.8s" /> And the man pulled off his mitten. <break time="0.8s" /> To tear the ice from its feet. <break time="0.8s" /> He bared his fingers. <break time="0.8s" /> For less than a minute. <break time="0.8s" /> But he was astonished. <break time="0.8s" /> At how quickly they became numb. <break time="0.8s" /> At half past twelve. <break time="0.8s" /> He reached the forks of the creek. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> To eat his lunch. <break time="0.8s" /> But the ice around his mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> Would not let him bite the biscuit. <break time="0.8s" /> For he had forgotten. <break time="0.8s" /> To build a fire first. <break time="0.8s" /> He remembered the old timer. <break time="0.8s" /> On Sulphur Creek. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had told him. <break time="0.8s" /> How cold it could get. <break time="0.8s" /> And he had laughed at him at the time. <break time="0.8s" /> So he built a small fire. <break time="0.8s" /> And sitting by its warmth. <break time="0.8s" /> He ate his biscuits. <break time="0.8s" /> While the dog lay happily. <break time="0.8s" /> Near the flames.
